index file and an http\\nprogram that supports random access.   The\\nwgrib inventory is used for the index file, and cURL is used for the random-access http program.  \\nBoth are freely\\navailable, widely used, work on many platforms and are easily\\nscripted/automated/put into a cronjob.  Two perl scripts are also\\nrequired, get_inf.pl and get_grib.pl,  which are downloadable from\\nthe NCEP CPC website (see \\\"Requirements\\\" below).\\n\\nThe basic format of the quick download is:\\n\\n   get_inv.pl INV_URL | grep FIELDS | get_grib.pl GRIB_URL OUTPUT\\n\\n- INV_URL is the URL of a wgrib inventory, for example:  \\n  http://nomad.ncep.noaa.gov/pub/data/nccf/com/gfs/prod/gfs.2008120200/gfs.t00z.pgrbf12.grib2.idx\\n- FIELDS is string that selects the desired fields (wgrib compatible), for example:  \\n  \\\":HGT:500 mb:\\\"\\n- GRIB_URL is the URL of the grib file, for example:   \\n  http://nomad.ncep.noaa.gov/pub/data/nccf/com/gfs/prod/gfs.2008120200/gfs.t00z.pgrbf12.grib2\\n- OUTPUT is the name of the for the downloaded grib file\\n\\nThe \\\"get_inv.pl INV_URL\\\" downloads the wgrib inventory off the net and adds\\na range field.\\n\\nThe \\\"grep FIELDS\\\" uses the grep command to select desired\\nfields from the inventory. Use of the \\\"grep FIELDS\\\" is similar to the\\nprocedure used when using wgrib to extract fields.\\n\\nThe \\\"get_grib.pl\\nGRIB_URL OUTPUT\\\" uses the filtered inventory to select the fields\\nfrom GRIB_URL to download. The selected fields are saved in OUTPUT.\\n\\nSee the\\nwgrib home page for more information and tricks on using grep and egrep.\\n\\n## Examples\\n\\n__This example downloads the the 500 mb height from the 12 hour (f12) from the 00Z (t00z)\\nGFS fcst from the NCEP NOMAD server:__\\n\\nINV_URL=\\\"http://nomad.ncep.noaa.gov/pub/data/nccf/com/gfs/prod/gfs.20081202100gfs.t00z.pgrbf12.grib2.idx\\\"  \\nGRIB_URL=\\\"http://nomad.ncep.noaa.gov/pub/data/nccf/com/gfs/prod/gfs.2008120200/gfs.t00z.pgrbf12.grib2\\\"  \\nget_inv.pl $INV_URL | grep \\\":HGT:500 mb:\\\" | get_grib.pl $GRIB_URL out.grb\\n\\n__This example is similar to the above example except it downloads both the\\n500 mb height and the 1000 mb temperature:__\\n\\nINV_URL=\\\"http://nomad.ncep.noaa.gov/pub/data/nccf/com/gfs/prod/gfs.20081202100gfs.t00z.pgrbf12.grib2.idx\\\"  \\nGRIB_URL=\\\"http://nomad.ncep.noaa.gov/pub/data/nccf/com/gfs/prod/gfs.2008120200/gfs.t00z.pgrbf12.grib2\\\"  \\nget_inv.pl $INV_URL| grep \\\"(:HGT:500 mb:|:TMP:1000 mb:)\\\" | get_grib.pl  $GRIB_URL out.grb\\n\\n__If you want to download multiple fields, for example, precipitation and 2 meter temperature, you\\ncan type,__\\n\\n     URL=\\\"http://nomads.ncep.noaa.gov/data/nccf/com/gfs/prod/gfs.2006070312/gfs.t12z.pgrb2f00.grib2\\\"  \\n     get_inv.pl $URL.idx | egrep ':(PRATE|TMP:2 m above gnd):' | get_grib.pl $URL out\\n\\nThe above code will put the precipiation and 2-m temp in the file \\\"out\\\". Egrep understands\\nregular expressions which is a very powerful feature.\\n\\n__If you are doing multiple downloads from the same file, you can save time by keeping a local\\ncopy of the inventory. For example:__   \\n     URL=\\\"http://nomads.ncep.noaa.gov/data/nccf/com/gfs/prod/gfs.2006070312/gfs.t12z.pgrb2f00.grib2\\\"  \\n     get_inv.pl $URL.idx > my_inv  \\n     grep \\\":UGRD:\\\" < my_inv | get_grib.pl $URL ugrd.grb  \\n     grep \\\":VGRD:\\\" < my_inv | get_grib.pl $URL vgrd.grb  \\n     grep \\\":TMP:\\\" < my_inv | get_grib.pl $URL tmp.grb  \\n   \\nThe above code saves two extra downloads of the inventory.\\n\\n## Requirements\\n\\n1. perl\\n2. grep\\n3. cURL\\n4. grib files and their wgrib inventory on an http server\\n5. get_inv.pl\\n6. get_grib.pl\\n\\n## Configuration (UNIX/Linux)\\n\\nThe first two lines of get_inv.pl and get_grib.pl need to be modified.\\nThe first line should point to your perl interpreter. The\\nsecond line needs to point to the location of curl if it is not\\non your path.\\n\\n## Usage: Windows\\n\\nThere have been some reports that the perl scripts didn't work on Windows machines. Depending on the dataset the API can format the data as comma-separated values (CSV), space-separated values (SSV), JavaScript Object Notation (JSON), Portable Document Format (PDF) and Network Common Data Form (NetCDF). The NCEI Access Data Service is only available via HTTP Strict Transport Security (HSTS) following Federal government policy.\\n\\n## Request Endpoint\\n\\nThe NCEI Access Data Service queries use HTTP 1.1 GET request and the endpoint is located off the base URL at __.../access/services/data/v1__.\\n\\n## Request Endpoint Parameters\\n\\nThe NCEI Access Data Service endpoint allows several parameters to select and retrieve data from available datasets. The request parameters are passed using a GET request. Some of these request parameters change based on the dataset parameter that is passed.\\n\\n### Datasets — dataset\\n\\nThe dataset parameter selects the dataset to query for data. Please note that all the datasets are __NOT__ available through the NCEI Access Data Service API, however new datasets are added quarterly.\\n\\n...__?dataset=daily-summaries__\\n\\n### Station Identifiers — stations\\n\\nThe stations parameter adds a comma separated list of station identifiers for selection and subsetting.\\n\\n...__&stations=USC00457180,USC00390043__\\n\\n### Start Date — startDate\\n\\nThis is the date to select from the dataset for a given start date. This parameter is an ISO 8601 date (YYYY-MM-DD) -or- ISO 8601 combined date and time format (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss). If using an ISO 8601 combined date and time format __the T that separates the time is NOT optional__. The ISO 8601 combined date and time also supports optional time zone representations.  Use Z or z for UTC and +HH:mm or -HH:mm for the offset from UTC. The plus symbol (+) must be URL encoded at “%2B” or it will not validate. The start and end dates are not required. The startDate must come before the endDate parameter. Some datasets are averages over time and may ignore parts of a date.\\n\\nISO 8601 date format example:\\n\\n__1776-07-04  \\n1941-12-07__\\n\\nISO 8601 combined date and time examples:\\n\\n__2001-11-02T12:45:00Z  \\n2001-11-02T12:45:00z  \\n2001-11-02T08:45:00+04:00__\\n\\n...__&startDate=1941-12-07T09:31:20z__\\n\\nFor UTC hour and minute offsets (HH:mm), the plus symbol (+) must be URL encoded as “%2B” or it will not validate:\\n\\n...__&startDate=2009-01-27T08:45:00%2B04:00__\\n\\n### End Date — endDate\\n\\nThis is the date to select datasets whose period of record (PoR) starts on or after the given endDate. This parameter is an ISO 8601 date (YYYY-MM-DD) -or- ISO 8601 combined date and time format (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss). If using an ISO 8601 combined date and time format, the T that separates the time is NOT optional. The ISO 8601 combined date and time also supports optional time zone representations.  Use Z or z for UTC and +HH:mm or -HH:mm for the offset from UTC. The plus symbol (+) must be URL encoded as “__%2B__” or it will not validate. __If the start date is required for the dataset then you must include the startDate parameter__.\\n\\n### Data Types, Observations/Variables — dataTypes\\n\\nData Types allows the selection of one or many dataTypes. Datasets have different names for the data types (e.g., variables, observations). The dataTypes parameter is used with a comma-separated list. This parameter is case-sensitive and will respond with an HTTPS __Status Code: 400 Bad Request__ and JSON with more information.\\n\\n...__&dataTypes=MLY-PRCP-NORMAL,MLY-TMIN-NORMAL__\\n\\n### Bounding Box (N,W,S,E) — bbox\\n\\nThe bounding box (bbox) is used to select data from a geographic location contained within the coordinates, given as four comma separated numbers. North and South range from -90 to 90 and East and West range from -180 to 180. If these are not set the geographic extent defaults to the entire globe (90,-180,-90,180).\\n\\n...__&bbox=49.795,-2.073,49.183,-0.992__\\n\\n### Data Format — format\\n\\nThe format parameter allows the user to select how the data should be formatted. Note that some data formats ignore certain data types. For example, PDF data may only display data types for a report, and not for the requested dataTypes.\\n\\nThese are the available formats:\\n\\n__csv__ — Comma-Separated Values (CSV)  \\n__ssv__ — Space-Separated Values (SSV)  \\n__json__ — JavaScript Object Notation (JSON)  \\n__pdf__ — Portable Document Format (PDF)  \\n__netcdf__  — Network Common Data Form (NetCDF)\\n\\n### Result Options — options\\n\\nThe API supports an options parameter that turns features on and off. Options are separated by commas and the respective values are separated by a colon (__:__); boolean values are represented by __true__ or __false__,or zero (__0__) and one (__1__). Options can either pass as a comma-separated list:\\n\\n…__&options=includeAttributes:true,includeStationName:1__\\n\\nor individually as URL parameters:\\n\\n...__&includeAttributes=0&includeStationName=true__\\n\\n### Display Data Attributes — includeAttributes\\n\\nIncludes the attribute for a selected datatype. These are typically comma separated (e.g., “__T,,0,0700__”), and added to the results if the __includeAttributes__ parameter is set to __true__. This value can be the word __true__ or a numeric representation of the boolean value, __1__. The default value is __false__ or __0__ and will not display datatype(s) attributes.\\n\\n...__&includeAttributes=true__\\n\\n### Include Station Name — includeStationName\\n\\nIncludes the station’s name, if available, for the selected dataset and data type. This value can be the word __true__ or a numeric representation of the boolean value, __1__. The default value is __false__ or __0__ and will not display datatype(s) attributes.\\n\\n…__&includeStationName=true__\\n\\n### Display Station Location — includeStationLocation\\n\\nIncludes the station’s location, if available, for the selected dataset and data type. This value can be the word __true__ or a numeric representation of the boolean value, __1__. The default value is __false__ or __0__ and will not display datatype(s) attributes.\\n\\n…__&includeStationLocation=1__\\n\\n### Converting Units — units\\n\\nThe units parameter converts the output data for datasets and datatypes that support conversion to either “__metric__” or “__standard__” units.\\n\\n## Example Requests\\n\\n### CSV (default):\\n\\n### PDF\\n\\n### JSON\\n\\n## Request Responses\\n\\nThe NCEI Access Search Service returns appropriate HTTP/1.1 status codes and response headers depending on the request and service status. For example, PDF data may only display data types for a report, and not for the requested dataTypes.\\n\\nThese are the available formats:\\n\\n__csv__ — Comma-Separated Values (CSV)  \\n__ssv__ — Space-Separated Values (SSV)  \\n__json__ — JavaScript Object Notation (JSON)  \\n__pdf__ — Portable Document Format (PDF)  \\n__netcdf__  — Network Common Data Form (NetCDF)\\n\\n### Result Options — options\\n\\nThe API supports an options parameter that turns features on and off. Options are separated by commas and the respective values are separated by a colon (__:__); boolean values are represented by __true__ or __false__,or zero (__0__) and one (__1__). Options can either pass as a comma-separated list:\\n\\n…__&options=includeAttributes:true,includeStationName:1__\\n\\nor individually as URL parameters:\\n\\n...__&includeAttributes=0&includeStationName=true__\\n\\n### Display Data Attributes — includeAttributes\\n\\nIncludes the attribute for a selected datatype. These are typically comma separated (e.g., “__T,,0,0700__”), and added to the results if the __includeAttributes__ parameter is set to __true__. This value can be the word __true__ or a numeric representation of the boolean value, __1__. The default value is __false__ or __0__ and will not display datatype(s) attributes.\\n\\n...__&includeAttributes=true__\\n\\n### Include Station Name — includeStationName\\n\\nIncludes the station’s name, if available, for the selected dataset and data type. This value can be the word __true__ or a numeric representation of the boolean value, __1__. The default value is __false__ or __0__ and will not display datatype(s) attributes.\\n\\n…__&includeStationName=true__\\n\\n### Display Station Location — includeStationLocation\\n\\nIncludes the station’s location, if available, for the selected dataset and data type. This value can be the word __true__ or a numeric representation of the boolean value, __1__. The default value is __false__ or __0__ and will not display datatype(s) attributes.\\n\\n…__&includeStationLocation=1__\\n\\n### Converting Units — units\\n\\nThe units parameter converts the output data for datasets and datatypes that support conversion to either “__metric__” or “__standard__” units.\\n\\n## Example Requests\\n\\n### CSV (default):\\n\\n### PDF\\n\\n### JSON\\n\\n## Request Responses\\n\\nThe NCEI Access Search Service returns appropriate HTTP/1.1 status codes and response headers depending on the request and service status. These responses follow RFC 2616 (Fielding, et al).\\n\\n### 400 - Bad Request\\n\\nThe request is malformed and needs to be modified in order to execute. All major archives provide public access without authentication requirements, with varying degrees of programmatic interface support.\n\n## Primary Archive Sources\n\n### 1. NCEI (National Centers for Environmental Information)\n\n**Organization:** National Centers for Environmental Information (NOAA)  \n**Primary Use:** Long-term archival and data services\n\n#### Access Methods\n- **REST API:** https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/access/services/data/v1\n- **Web Portal:** https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/access/search/dataset-search/\n- **Documentation:** [NCEI Data Service API User Documentation](https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/support/access-data-service-api-user-documentation)\n\n#### Technical Details\n- **Base URL:** `https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/access/services/data/v1`\n- **Authentication:** None required (public HTTPS)\n- **Protocol:** HTTP 1.1 GET requests\n- **Data Formats:** CSV, SSV, JSON, PDF, NetCDF\n- **HSTS:** Enforced following Federal government policy\n\n#### Temporal Coverage\n- Varies by dataset\n- Some datasets dating back to 1901\n- Quarterly additions of new datasets\n- Data transitioned from NOMADS after ~1 month\n\n#### Programmatic Access\n- Full REST API with parameter-based queries\n- Support for bounding box spatial selection (bbox=N,W,S,E)\n- Date range selection (startDate, endDate)\n- Station selection for station-based datasets\n- Multiple output formats\n\n#### Browse/Search Interface\n- Comprehensive web portal at [NCEI Search](https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/access/search/dataset-search/)\n- ~110 separate data sources updated daily\n- Filter by dataset, station, date range, and data types\n\n#### Key Parameters\n```http\n?dataset=daily-summaries\n&stations=USC00457180,USC00390043\n&startDate=2001-11-02T12:45:00Z\n&endDate=2024-01-01T00:00:00Z\n&dataTypes=MLY-PRCP-NORMAL,MLY-TMIN-NORMAL\n&bbox=49.795,-2.073,49.183,-0.992\n&format=csv\n&includeAttributes=true\n```\n\n---\n\n### 2. NOMADS (NOAA Operational Model Archive and Distribution System)\n\n**Organization:** National Centers for Environmental Prediction (NCEP)  \n**Primary Use:** Recent operational model data distribution\n\n#### Access Methods\n- **Main Portal:** https://nomads.ncep.noaa.gov/\n- **Fast GRIB2 Download:** [Partial HTTP Transfers Documentation](https://nomads.ncep.noaa.gov/info.php?page=fastdownload)\n- **GRIB Filter Web App:** For subsetting and repackaging GRIB2 files\n\n#### Technical Details\n- **Base URL:** `https://nomads.ncep.noaa.gov/`\n- **Authentication:** None required (public HTTP/HTTPS)\n- **Protocol:** HTTP random access with index files\n- **Data Format:** Primarily GRIB2 (some GRIB legacy)\n- **Tools:** wgrib, wgrib2, cURL, perl scripts\n\n#### Temporal Coverage\n- **Recent data:** Up to approximately 1 month\n- **Older data:** Transitions to NCEI archives\n- **Data retention:** Operational models retained for ~30 days\n- **Archive transition:** Automatic transfer to NCEI\n\n#### Programmatic Access\n\n**Method 1: Fast Download with Partial HTTP Transfers**\n\nRequires index files (`.idx`) and HTTP program supporting random access:\n\n```bash\n# Basic pattern:\nget_inv.pl INV_URL | grep FIELDS | get_grib.pl GRIB_URL OUTPUT\n\n# Example: Download 500mb height from GFS forecast\nINV_URL=\"http://nomads.ncep.noaa.gov/pub/data/nccf/com/gfs/prod/gfs.2008120200/gfs.t00z.pgrbf12.grib2.idx\"\nGRIB_URL=\"http://nomads.ncep.noaa.gov/pub/data/nccf/com/gfs/prod/gfs.2008120200/gfs.t00z.pgrbf12.grib2\"\nget_inv.pl $INV_URL | grep \":HGT:500 mb:\" | get_grib.pl $GRIB_URL out.grb\n```\n\n**Requirements:**\n- perl\n- grep\n- cURL with HTTP range support\n- grib files with wgrib inventory index\n- `get_inv.pl` and `get_grib.pl` scripts\n\n**Method 2: Direct API Access**\nDifferent models have different API endpoints (GFS, GEM, etc.)\n\n#### Browse/Search Interface\n- Main NOMADS portal provides data access method matrix\n- Data Set field contains description and availability information\n- Column headings describe each access method\n\n#### Model Coverage\n- GFS (Global Forecast System)\n- GDAS (Global Data Assimilation System)\n- GFS Wave Model\n- Various regional and specialized models\n\n---\n\n### 3. NOAA Big Data Project / NODD (Open Data Dissemination)\n\n**Organization:** NOAA Open Data Dissemination Program  \n**Primary Use:** Cloud-native access to petabyte-scale NOAA datasets\n\n#### Access Methods\n- **AWS Registry:** [Registry of Open Data on AWS - NOAA](https://registry.opendata.aws/collab/noaa/)\n- **Direct S3 Access:** Public S3 buckets (no AWS credentials required)\n- **Documentation:** [NOAA NODD Program Information](https://www.noaa.gov/information-technology/open-data-dissemination)\n\n#### Cloud Platforms\n- **Amazon Web Services (AWS)** - Primary platform\n- **Microsoft Azure**\n- **Google Cloud Platform**\n\n#### Technical Details\n- **Authentication:** None required for public data (AWS: anonymous access)\n- **Protocol:** S3 API (AWS), equivalent for Azure/GCP\n- **Data Format:** Primarily GRIB2, some ZARR/NetCDF\n- **Access Speed:** Cloud-native, high-bandwidth\n\n#### Key GRIB2 Datasets on AWS\n\n| Dataset | S3 Bucket | Temporal Coverage | Resolution |\n|---------|-----------|-------------------|------------|\n| GFS (Global Forecast System) | `noaa-gfs-bdp-pds` | 2019-present | 0.25° global |\n| NBM (National Blend of Models) | `noaa-nbm-grib2-pds` | 2021-present | CONUS ~3km |\n| HRRR (High-Resolution Rapid Refresh) | `noaa-hrrr-bdp-pds` | 2015-present | 3km CONUS |\n| GEFS (Global Ensemble Forecast System) | `noaa-gefs-bdp-pds` | 2019-present | Ensemble |\n| RTMA/URMA | Various buckets | 2003-present | ~2.5km CONUS |\n\n#### Direct S3 Access Examples\n\n```bash\n# List GFS data in S3 bucket (no AWS credentials needed)\naws s3 ls s3://noaa-gfs-bdp-pds/ --no-sign-request\n\n# Access specific GFS GRIB2 file\nhttps://noaa-gfs-bdp-pds.s3.amazonaws.com/gfs.20240101/00/atmos/gfs.t00z.pgrb2.0p25.f000\n\n# NBM GRIB2 file\nhttps://noaa-nbm-grib2-pds.s3.amazonaws.com/nbm.20240101/00/nbm.t00z.conusnest.02.500mb.grib2\n```\n\n#### Temporal Coverage by Dataset\n- **GFS:** 2019-present (near real-time, 4 cycles/day)\n- **HRRR:** 2015-present (hourly updates)\n- **NBM:** 2021-present (hourly, CONUS)\n- **GEFS:** 2019-present (ensemble members)\n- **Climate reanalysis:** Multi-decade datasets available\n\n#### Programmatic Access\n- Direct S3 API calls (anonymous access)\n- AWS CLI with `--no-sign-request`\n- Python boto3 with anonymous configuration\n- Community tools: Herbie package, HRRR-B package\n- Sample notebooks: [NOAA GFS Quickstart](https://github.com/aws-samples/aws-opendata-samples/blob/main/notebooks/noaa-gfs/noaa_gfs_quickstart.ipynb)\n\n#### Browse/Search Interface\n- [AWS S3 Explorer for GFS](https://noaa-gfs-bdp-pds.s3.amazonaws.com/index.html)\n- [NODD Dataset Registry](https://www.noaa.gov/nodd/datasets)\n- Quarterly updates to dataset registry\n\n---\n\n### 4. NCEP Products (Direct Model Output)\n\n**Organization:** National Centers for Environmental Prediction  \n**Primary Use:** Direct access to operational model products\n\n#### Access Methods\n- **Products Page:** [NCEP GFS and GDAS Products](https://www.nco.ncep.noaa.gov/pmb/products/gfs/)\n- **FTP Server:** ftp://ftpprd.ncep.noaa.gov/\n- **HTTP Server:** http://www.nco.ncep.noaa.gov/pmb/data/\n\n#### Technical Details\n- **Base URLs:**\n  - FTP: `ftp://ftpprd.ncep.noaa.gov/pub/data/nccf/com/gfs/prod/`\n  - HTTP: `http://nomads.ncep.noaa.gov/pub/data/nccf/com/gfs/prod/`\n- **Authentication:** None (anonymous FTP/public HTTP)\n- **Protocol:** FTP, HTTP\n- **Data Format:** GRIB2\n\n#### Temporal Coverage\n- **Operational:** Real-time, latest model runs\n- **Archive:** Varies by model (typically days to weeks)\n- **Long-term:** Transitions to NCEI\n\n#### Model Coverage\n- GFS (Global Forecast System)\n- GDAS (Global Data Assimilation System)\n- GFS Wave Model\n- NAM (North American Mesoscale)\n- RAP (Rapid Refresh)\n- HRRR (High-Resolution Rapid Refresh)\n\n#### Programmatic Access\n- Standard FTP clients\n- wget/curl for HTTP\n- Index file-based subsetting (as documented in NOMADS section)\n- Direct file path construction\n\n---\n\n### 5. NOAA READY Archives\n\n**Organization:** NOAA Air Resources Laboratory  \n**Primary Use:** Archived model output for atmospheric dispersion modeling\n\n#### Access Methods\n- **Web Portal:** [READY Gridded Data Archives](https://www.ready.noaa.gov/archives.php)\n- **Documentation:** Integrated with READY system\n\n#### Technical Details\n- **Access Method:** Web interface + direct HTTP\n- **Authentication:** None required\n- **Data Format:** Reprocessed GRIB format\n\n#### Temporal Coverage\n- Varies by model\n- Focus on meteorological data for dispersion modeling\n- Archive extends beyond NOMADS retention period\n\n---\n\n### 6. Additional NOAA GRIB2 Sources\n\n#### NOAA Earthdata (NASA Partnership)\n- **Portal:** [NOAA Earthdata - NCEP GFS 0.25 Degree](https://access.earthdata.nasa.gov/collections/C1214110986-SCIOPS)\n- registration)\n\n#### University of Utah HRRR Archive\n- **Format:** ZARR (cloud-optimized)\n- **Access:** Via AWS or direct download\n- **Documentation:** Referenced in AWS HRRR dataset Sample notebooks: [NOAA GFS Quickstart](https://github.com/aws-samples/aws-opendata-samples/blob/main/notebooks/noaa-gfs/noaa_gfs_quickstart.ipynb)\n\n#### Browse/Search Interface\n- [AWS S3 Explorer for GFS](https://noaa-gfs-bdp-pds.s3.amazonaws.com/index.html)\n- [NODD Dataset Registry](https://www.noaa.gov/nodd/datasets)\n- Quarterly updates to dataset registry\n\n---\n\n### 4. NCEP Products (Direct Model Output)\n\n**Organization:** National Centers for Environmental Prediction  \n**Primary Use:** Direct access to operational model products\n\n#### Access Methods\n- **Products Page:** [NCEP GFS and GDAS Products](https://www.nco.ncep.noaa.gov/pmb/products/gfs/)\n- **FTP Server:** ftp://ftpprd.ncep.noaa.gov/\n- **HTTP Server:** http://www.nco.ncep.noaa.gov/pmb/data/\n\n#### Technical Details\n- **Base URLs:**\n  - FTP: `ftp://ftpprd.ncep.noaa.gov/pub/data/nccf/com/gfs/prod/`\n  - HTTP: `http://nomads.ncep.noaa.gov/pub/data/nccf/com/gfs/prod/`\n- **Authentication:** None (anonymous FTP/public HTTP)\n- **Protocol:** FTP, HTTP\n- **Data Format:** GRIB2\n\n#### Temporal Coverage\n- **Operational:** Real-time, latest model runs\n- **Archive:** Varies by model (typically days to weeks)\n- **Long-term:** Transitions to NCEI\n\n#### Model Coverage\n- GFS (Global Forecast System)\n- GDAS (Global Data Assimilation System)\n- GFS Wave Model\n- NAM (North American Mesoscale)\n- RAP (Rapid Refresh)\n- HRRR (High-Resolution Rapid Refresh)\n\n#### Programmatic Access\n- Standard FTP clients\n- wget/curl for HTTP\n- Index file-based subsetting (as documented in NOMADS section)\n- Direct file path construction\n\n---\n\n### 5. NOAA READY Archives\n\n**Organization:** NOAA Air Resources Laboratory  \n**Primary Use:** Archived model output for atmospheric dispersion modeling\n\n#### Access Methods\n- **Web Portal:** [READY Gridded Data Archives](https://www.ready.noaa.gov/archives.php)\n- **Documentation:** Integrated with READY system\n\n#### Technical Details\n- **Access Method:** Web interface + direct HTTP\n- **Authentication:** None required\n- **Data Format:** Reprocessed GRIB format\n\n#### Temporal Coverage\n- Varies by model\n- Focus on meteorological data for dispersion modeling\n- Archive extends beyond NOMADS retention period\n\n---\n\n### 6. Additional NOAA GRIB2 Sources\n\n#### NOAA Earthdata (NASA Partnership)\n- **Portal:** [NOAA Earthdata - NCEP GFS 0.25 Degree](https://access.earthdata.nasa.gov/collections/C1214110986-SCIOPS)\n- registration)\n\n#### University of Utah HRRR Archive\n- **Format:** ZARR (cloud-optimized)\n- **Access:** Via AWS or direct download\n- **Documentation:** Referenced in AWS HRRR dataset details\n\n#### NOAA ISD (Integrated Surface Database)\n- **AWS Registry:** [NOAA ISD Dataset](https://registry.opendata.aws/noaa-isd/)\n- **Coverage:** Global hourly observations from 35,000+ stations\n- **Temporal:** Some data back to 1901\n- **Format:** gzipped fixed width (not GRIB, but related surface obs)\n\n---\n\n## Summary Table of Primary GRIB2 Sources\n\n| Source | Access Method
